challenge.better_approach: Deleting preflight's hollow half in favour of bin/cairn test --hollow was looked at; --hollow needs the chart's writes_to and a crossed BUILDME, and preflight is the earlier, cheaper check run before PROVEME. Fixing the one line keeps the cheap check honest.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That git checkout <pre> -- <files> fails as a whole when one path is absent at <pre>; measured on b7068 (the fallback ran and verdict.py stayed at HEAD).
challenge.prior_art: bin/cairn test --hollow reverts per file through the journal; this is the same per-file rule in a 10-line script, so it does not rebuild the tester.

answers.falsifier: Done when, over a scratch build that modifies m and adds n, the revert leaves m at its pre-build bytes and n gone, a modify-only build reverts too, and preflight.sh calls revert_build.sh. Wrong intent if bin/cairn test --hollow already serves every preflight caller, making preflight's revert dead weight.
answers.from_idea: none, because it was measured on ticket b7068b1ba431 in cairn/devices/cc/scripts/preflight.sh (its revert left verdict.py at HEAD)
answers.how: The revert moves out of preflight.sh into cairn/devices/cc/scripts/revert_build.sh <pre> <files...>, which per file checks it out from <pre> when it exists there and removes it otherwise; preflight.sh calls it. A proof runs it in a scratch git repo over a build that modifies one file and adds another.
answers.traces_to: Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass): a revert that leaves the build in place makes the hollow reading green, the false green a peer leans on.
answers.what: preflight's build-reverted run reverts every build file to the pre-build commit, the changed files as well as the new ones, so its hollow reading is never falsely green.

bullets.text: preflight.sh's `git checkout $PRE -- files || <rm new files>` reverts nothing when any file is new: the checkout fails whole and the fallback only deletes. Its reverted run read teeth 1, 2, 4 green on b7068.
